name: lagsmith-mcp

tools.name: list_targets
tools.description: List running simulators and the apps installed on them, running Mac apps, the presets, and the current rules.

tools.name: status
tools.description: Show every rule, what it's doing, and whether Lagsmith's proxy is running.

tools.name: set_network
tools.description: Slow down or break one app's network, and only that app's. Creates the rule if needed and turns it on. Combine a preset with exact values or a failure mode.

after.description: For drop: seconds before a connection is cut.

app.description: The app: a bundle ID like com.me.MyApp, an app name, or * for every app in a simulator.

down.description: Download bandwidth in kilobits per second.

failure.description: airplane: every connection fails at once. refuse: refuse a percent of new connections. timeout: connections never answer. drop: cut connections after some seconds. outages: go offline and back repeatedly.

hosts.description: Comma-separated hosts to limit the rule to, like api.me.com,*.cdn.me.com.

hosts_mode.description: only (default): just those hosts; except: everything but them.

percent.description: For refuse: the percent of connections refused.

preset.description: No Throttling, Edge, 3G, DSL, LTE, WiFi, Very Bad Network, 100% Loss, or a saved preset.

simulator.description: For iOS Simulator apps: booted, any, a device name or a UDID. Leave out for a Mac app.

up.description: Upload bandwidth in kilobits per second.

tools.name: reset_network
tools.description: Put an app back to full speed with no failures, host limits or endpoint rules. It stays watched, so its requests still show.

app.description: The app: a bundle ID like com.me.MyApp, an app name, or * for every app in a simulator.

simulator.description: For iOS Simulator apps: booted, any, a device name or a UDID. Leave out for a Mac app.

tools.name: stop_watching
tools.description: Turn off an app's rule. Its traffic goes back to normal and stops being watched.

app.description: The app: a bundle ID like com.me.MyApp, an app name, or * for every app in a simulator.

simulator.description: For iOS Simulator apps: booted, any, a device name or a UDID. Leave out for a Mac app.

tools.name: relaunch_app
tools.description: Quit and reopen a simulator app with request monitoring, so every connection it makes goes through its rule and its requests are recorded. Do this after the first set_network for an app that was already running.

app.description: The app: a bundle ID like com.me.MyApp, an app name, or * for every app in a simulator.

simulator.description: For iOS Simulator apps: booted, any, a device name or a UDID. Leave out for a Mac app.

tools.name: get_requests
tools.description: A simulator app's recent HTTP requests, newest first: method, URL, status, errors, time, and optionally bodies. Needs the app to have been launched with request monitoring (relaunch_app).

app.description: The app: a bundle ID like com.me.MyApp, an app name, or * for every app in a simulator.

filter.description: A search: words, or filters like status:4xx, method:POST, host:api, path:/v1, is:failed, -host:cdn.

include_bodies.description: Include request and response bodies (up to 4,000 characters each).

simulator.description: For iOS Simulator apps: booted, any, a device name or a UDID. Leave out for a Mac app.

tools.name: fail_endpoint
tools.description: Make requests to one endpoint fail inside a simulator app while the rest of the app works.

app.description: The app: a bundle ID like com.me.MyApp, an app name, or * for every app in a simulator.

kind.description: offline: fails as no internet. timeout: times out. status: answers with an HTTP status. delay: sent after a wait.

pattern.description: Requests whose URL contains this, like api.me.com/v1/feed. Use * for any text.

simulator.description: For iOS Simulator apps: booted, any, a device name or a UDID. Leave out for a Mac app.

value.description: For status: the HTTP status (default 500). For delay: seconds (default 3). For timeout: at most this many seconds.

tools.name: mock_endpoint
tools.description: Answer requests to one endpoint in a simulator app with a made-up response, without reaching the server.

app.description: The app: a bundle ID like com.me.MyApp, an app name, or * for every app in a simulator.

pattern.description: Requests whose URL contains this, like api.me.com/v1/user. Use * for any text.

simulator.description: For iOS Simulator apps: booted, any, a device name or a UDID. Leave out for a Mac app.

tools.description: Remove an app's endpoint failures and mocks: all of them, or those for one pattern.

instructions:
Lagsmith runs on macOS only (macOS 13 Ventura or later). See https://lagsmith.com/download.

Lagsmith slows down and breaks the network of individual apps on this Mac: iOS Simulator apps and Mac apps. Only the apps you target are affected, so your own connection, the terminal and test runners stay at full speed. Use it to test how an app copes with a slow or failing network, for example before or during end-to-end and UI tests.

Typical flow: list_targets to find the app's bundle ID and simulator; set_network with a preset like 3G or a failure like airplane; relaunch_app so every connection the app makes goes through the new conditions (needed the first time, and gives request monitoring); run the tests or use the app; get_requests to see what the app actually sent and got back; reset_network when done. fail_endpoint and mock_endpoint break or fake one endpoint while the rest works.

For simulator apps pass simulator: "booted" (the running simulator), a device name or a UDID. Leave simulator out for a Mac app.

Airplane mode in a simulator app launched with relaunch_app acts like a device's, within about 2 seconds: requests fail with NSURLErrorNotConnectedToInternet (-1009), NWPathMonitor reports an unsatisfied path and calls its handler, and SCNetworkReachability reports no network. The app also gets an in-app notification "LagsmithNetworkDidChange" (userInfo["offline"]: Bool).
